subject: Re: Nordholm Payments — EU-only Hosted API data residency enforcement follow-up
body:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Bergström <lena.bergstrom@nordholm-payments.eu>
Cc: Jonas Richter <jonas.richter@nordholm-payments.eu>
Date: Thu, Feb 6, 2025 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Nordholm Payments — EU-only Hosted API data residency enforcement follow-up

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the security review on Tuesday. Following up with the specific items you asked for re: EU-only processing on our Hosted API.

1) Residency FAQ / narrative
Attached is our current “Data Residency Enforcement FAQ” (v1.2). It covers what we pin, what we don’t (yet), and what evidence we can provide during procurement.

2) Planned enforcement behavior (EU-only)
Here’s the intended behavior for “EU-only” (allowed regions = EU; primary region = eu-central):
- Requests are evaluated at request-time against your org/project (and optionally API key) residency policy.
- Routing will only select EU regions; cross-region fallback is blocked by default.
- If a request would route outside EU, we fail deterministically with a policy error (not a generic 5xx).
- Logging/tracing/audit events are scoped to the pinned region(s). We log the residency decision context (policy evaluated, selected region, and block reason) without moving prompt/content across regions.

3) Error handling
On block, the response will include:
- HTTP status: 409
- Machine-readable error code: residency_policy_violation
- request_id for support correlation
- A short “how to fix” message pointing to the pinned/allowed region config

If helpful, we can also share an example payload (same structure streaming + non-streaming).

Next step
Would you like to set up a 30-min technical deep dive next week? I can bring our product owner for Security & Compliance to walk through policy configuration + enforcement boundaries.

A few options (your time):
- Tue 11 Feb: 15:00–16:00 CET
- Wed 12 Feb: 10:00–10:30 CET
- Thu 13 Feb: 14:00–15:00 CET

Best,
Avery

—
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com


From: Lena Bergström <lena.bergstrom@nordholm-payments.eu>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Richter <jonas.richter@nordholm-payments.eu>
Date: Thu, Feb 6, 2025 at 18:41 CET
Subject: Re: Nordholm Payments — EU-only Hosted API data residency enforcement follow-up

Hi Avery,

Thanks — received the FAQ.

Two quick clarifications before we schedule:
1) When you say “blocked by default,” does that also include automatic model fallback (e.g., if the EU region is saturated)? We need a hard guarantee that prompts never leave EU.
2) Can we get confirmation that support tooling (debug logs / console) won’t display or move content outside the EU either? We’ve been burned by “control plane is US-based” caveats elsewhere.

Timing: Wed 12 Feb 10:00–10:30 CET works.

Regards,
Lena

—
Lena Bergström
Head of Security & Risk
Nordholm Payments


From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Bergström <lena.bergstrom@nordholm-payments.eu>
Cc: Jonas Richter <jonas.richter@nordholm-payments.eu>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 6, 2025 at 10:27 AM PST
Subject: Re: Nordholm Payments — EU-only Hosted API data residency enforcement follow-up

Hi Lena —

Great questions. Looping in Naomi Feldman (Product owner, Security & Compliance) so you can hear the enforcement boundaries directly.

1) Fallback / saturation
Yes — the intent is that “blocked by default” includes cross-region fallback for capacity and model-variant fallback that would otherwise jump regions. With EU-only policies we will not route requests to a non-EU region, even if that means failing fast.

2) Support + tooling boundaries
For Hosted, the enforcement scope includes routing + request handling + logs/traces used for operations. The goal is that customer content (prompts, outputs, and derived content) does not move outside the pinned region set. We can walk through exactly what we store where and what metadata is permitted to be global.

Wed 12 Feb 10:00–10:30 CET is on hold. I’ll send a calendar invite shortly.

Best,
Avery


From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lena Bergström <lena.bergstrom@nordholm-payments.eu>
Cc: Jonas Richter <jonas.richter@nordholm-payments.eu>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 7, 2025 at 8:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Nordholm Payments — EU-only Hosted API data residency enforcement follow-up

Hi Lena,

Calendar invite sent for:
Wed 12 Feb 2025 — 10:00–10:30 CET
Video: Redwood Meet (link in invite)

Proposed agenda:
- Policy model (org vs project vs API key) + configuration
- Request-time enforcement + routing behavior (including failover)
- Error contract + troubleshooting workflow (request_id, error_code)
- Audit log events for policy changes and overrides

If you can share your target regions (Frankfurt vs Dublin preference) and any internal nomenclature you need to map to, Naomi can come prepared.

Thanks,
Avery


From: Lena Bergström <lena.bergstrom@nordholm-payments.eu>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Richter <jonas.richter@nordholm-payments.eu>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 10, 2025 at 16:37 CET
Subject: Re: Nordholm Payments — EU-only Hosted API data residency enforcement follow-up

Confirmed, thank you.

Preference is Frankfurt (eu-central) as primary, with EU-only allowed regions. We do not want any non-EU fallback.

One additional ask for the session: can you outline what evidence you can provide for auditors (SOC2/ISO narratives, screenshots, logs) specifically for “residency enforcement enabled” tenants?

See you Wednesday.

Regards,
Lena
